subject: Critical Thinking
title: Reductio ad Absurdum: Defeating Arguments by Their Own Logic
description: A quick, practical guide to Reductio ad Absurdum: Defeating Arguments by Their Own Logic.

hook.text: 'If your logic is correct, then it leads to this absurd conclusion.

buildup.text: Reductio ad absurdum: accept the opponent's premises, follow their logic, & show it leads to a contradiction or.

discovery.text: Example: 'If all opinions are equally valid, then the opinion that not all opinions are equally valid is also valid –.

twist.text: It's devastatingly effective because you use the opponent's OWN assumptions against them. No external evidence needed.

climax.text: Galileo used it: if heavy objects fall faster, then a combined heavy+light object should fall both faster AND slower.

punchline.text: Don't fight their argument. Follow it to its absurd conclusion.

quiz.question: How does reductio ad absurdum work?
options: By making fun of the opponent
By accepting the opponent's premises and showing they lead to a contradiction

details.summary: Reductio ad absurdum defeats an argument by showing that its premises lead to an absurd or contradictory conclusion. If following the logic produces nonsense, the starting assumption must be wrong.
details.whyItMatters: This technique lets you disprove claims without needing counter-evidence — the argument's own logic does the work for you.
takeaways: Reductio shows an argument's premises lead to contradiction
It requires no external evidence to work
It has been a pillar of logic since ancient Greece

faq.question: Can you give a simple example of reductio ad absurdum?
faq.answer: Assume there is a largest prime number. Then multiply all primes together and add one. This new number cannot be divided by any known prime, contradicting the assumption. So there must be infinitely many primes.

faq.question: How is reductio different from simply disagreeing with an argument?
faq.answer: Reductio uses the opponent's own premises to generate an absurd conclusion, proving the original claim false. Simple disagreement offers a competing view without internal refutation.
